guide: Open Start and type your imprint name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the cash floor, the months a title should take to earn back its cost and the payback months that make a new edition a go.
Check Team and Cost Categories. They hold your contractors and your typical rate for each kind of job; every quote is set against them.
Write each job in Jobs: title, kind, contractor, quote, units, dates and what you paid. The balance, days late and the overdue flag fill in by themselves.
Write each payment in Job Payments: deposit, milestone or final, with its date and status. Open payments show in Invoices Due against your cash floor.
Keep Titles and Editions up to date with price, print cost and royalty share (check each store's current terms).
Type copies sold and royalties earned for each edition in Cost per Edition, and the royalties of each month in Royalties by Month. Cost per Title, Payback by Title and Break-Even by Series fill in.
Type the closing cash of each month in Cash by Month. The invoice tests and the dashboard use it.
Read Overdue and Unpaid Jobs and Invoices Due every week and use the message links to chase a contractor or send a payment note.
Use Edition Go or No-go and Translation Cases to weigh a new edition before you order the work. Royalties and copies are your own estimates until the payment arrives.
Use the 18 calculators to test a title's payback, solve break-even copies, rank budgets, test cash, check quotes and plan stage payments.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
A first-time author with 1 to 3 books can use most sheets with a few rows; a small press can read the pen-name columns as author columns.
Read the Production KPI Dashboard and the charts every month. The workbook has no macros and works in Excel and Google Sheets.

listing.title: Author and Self-Publisher Production Costs and Break-Even Excel Template: Contractor Jobs, Payback, Audio Go or No-go
listing.headline: Know what each book cost and when it earns that back
listing.description:
Run the production side of an independent publishing business in one Excel workbook. Built for an author-publisher who pays editors, a cover designer, a formatter, narrators and a translator per job and wants to know what each title cost and when it earns that back.

The Jobs ledger holds every quote, units, due date, what was paid and the balance, with days late and an overdue flag. Job Payments records deposits, milestones and final payments, and Invoices Due lists the open ones nearest first with the cash left after paying them against your cash floor. Budget vs Actual sets every quote against your typical rate for that kind of job, and Unit Cost Check shows the cost per 1,000 words and per finished hour against your own average.

Cost per Title and Cost per Edition split the production cost, Payback by Title compares it with royalties to date and your own monthly average, and Break-Even by Series shows the copies each format needs. 18 calculators cover the title payback verdict, break-even copies, budget ranking, the invoice cash test, audio, large print and hardcover go or no-go, the translation business case, translate or write, stage payments, contractor concentration, quote choice, late job impact, a cost cap, a series budget, a cover refresh and a payback what-if. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to editors, the cover designer, the formatter, narrators, the translator, your assistant and your accountant.

This is part two of the Author and Self-Publisher Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data and a blank copy. It helps you keep track of your costs; royalties and copies are estimates until the payment arrives and nothing here promises sales. Confirm tax and contract points with your adviser.
